questions.title: Who will succeed Brendon McCullum as permanent head coach of England's men's Test team?
questions.background: Brendon McCullum currently coaches England's men's Test cricket team.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official England and Wales Cricket Board appointment announcement or reliable contemporaneous reporting of that announcement. Resolution : Resolve to the first person formally appointed as McCullum's permanent successor as head coach of England's men's Test team. Interim appointments and appointments solely concerning limited-overs cricket do not count. Resolution occurs when the appointment is announced, even if the coach begins work later. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed coach's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-17 update: frontrunner Andy Flower publicly and formally ruled himself out of the England Test head coach race at London Spirit's media day (BBC Sport, Sky Sports, Reuters, ESPNcricinfo, Hindustan Times), confirming he turned down the ECB even with dual-role IPL flexibility because IPL/RCB duties clash with the early English summer. Following Flower's withdrawal, iNews Cricket Correspondent Chris Stocks reports on July 17 that the ECB is now pivoting to former Australia coach Justin Langer as its top target (rated 4/5; strong Ashes rebuilding pedigree and county familiarity, though tempered by LSG IPL ties and past intensity concerns), lifting Langer 0.13 -> 0.26. Newly available Stephen Fleming (co-rated 4/5 by iNews, named by BBC Sport July 17) rises 0.19 -> 0.25 as he just left CSK after 18 years—removing the IPL clash that deterred Flower—was Rob Key's 2022 preference, and publicly welcomed an approach this week. Among remaining shortlisted contenders, Jonathan Trott (0.15 -> 0.16, English, available, named by BBC Sport/iNews 3/5), Richard Dawson (0.07 -> 0.09, English, ECB pathway, named by BBC Sport July 17), and Tom Moody (new entry at 0.07, explicitly named by BBC Sport July 17 alongside Trott, Dawson, and Fleming) round out the top 5, leaving 17% residual for Kumar Sangakkara, Mike Hesson, Adi Birrell, and unlisted options as BBC notes the ECB is still in an initial stage and open to an interim for August's Pakistan series.

questions.background: The Democratic Republic of Congo declared an Ebola outbreak in May 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : WHO public statements about the DRC Ebola outbreak, including statements quoted in contemporaneous reputable news reporting. Resolution Window : Resolve to the province explicitly identified by WHO as experiencing surging weekly Ebola cases in its outbreak assessment publicly reported between September 10 and September 16, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: Key 2026-07-14 to 2026-07-16 WHO, Reuters, Bloomberg, and Al Jazeera updates show the DRC Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak accelerating to 2,073 confirmed cases and 796 deaths (doubling deaths in two weeks; true scale estimated 2-4x higher with >80% unlinked cases across 5 provinces) and reveal a major correction needed on North Kivu. Bloomberg/Straits Times (July 15) reported that isolation facilities in North Kivu are ALREADY operating at over 120% occupancy—showing that despite M23 containing southern Goma, active overflow is hitting northern North Kivu right across the highway corridor from Ituri, where an angry mob attacked Nyakunde Hospital on July 15 (forcing Samaritan's Purse to evacuate and up to 10 Ebola patients to flee) alongside pay strikes shutting Bunia General Hospital and halting Rwampara safe burials. Restoring North Kivu sharply 0.16 -> 0.22. Holding Ituri at 0.34 (>90% of current cases per WHO July 14, with containment collapsing, though two months remain until mid-September). Trimming Tshopo slightly 0.30 -> 0.27 (still major #2 urban explosion threat in 1.5M-pop Kisangani on the Congo River, though confirmed cases remain low so far) and Haut-Uele 0.12 -> 0.10 (IRC warns of cross-border spread toward South Sudan), with South Kivu at 0.02 and 5% residual for Kinshasa/Bas-Uele/Maniema.

local_articles.title: Wimbledon finalist Muchova to miss Canadian Open after minor surgery
local_articles.snippet: July 19 - Wimbledon finalist Karolina Muchova said on Saturday she would miss next month's Canadian Open after undergoing minor surgery. The 29-year-old Czech lost to compatriot Linda Noskova 6-2 5-7 6-3 in the Wimbledon final earlier this month. It was the second Grand Slam final defeat of Muchova's career, following her loss to Poland's Iga Swiatek at the 2023 French Open. "I had to undergo a small surgery that will keep me off the court for a few weeks. Everything went well, and I'm already working on my recovery," Muchova posted on social media. "Sad to be missing Toronto this year. I was really looking forward to making my debut there, but recovery comes first." The world number six has struggled with a series of injury setbacks during her career, including recurring wrist problems. local_articles.snippet: Italian teenager Kimi Antonelli ended a three-race winless streak on Sunday to extend his lead in the Formula One drivers’ championship with a solid fighting victory for Mercedes in the Belgian Grand Prix. questions.current_reasoning: Updating stale June 28 Zandvoort forecast (7 weeks out, first race after the August summer break) to incorporate Silverstone Sprint, Qualifying, and July 5 British GP evidence (Reuters, Guardian). Ferrari's Silverstone upgrade package produced a major breakthrough—Charles Leclerc won from P2 on the grid (Ferrari's second GP win in three races) and Lewis Hamilton took Sprint pole/P2 plus GP P3 despite a 5s jump-start penalty and safety-car pit miscalculation—elevating Hamilton +0.03 (0.12 -> 0.15) and bringing Leclerc into #4 at 0.12 (replacing Lando Norris). Winless McLaren drops just outside the top five (~0.085 Norris, ~0.07 Piastri) after Norris admitted at Silverstone they were 0.7s/lap off and lacked downforce/slow-speed corner grip (crucial at Zandvoort), though McLaren's 2024-25 Zandvoort wins and 7 weeks of mid-season development keep substantial mass outside the top five. Mercedes remains season benchmark (9/9 poles, 7/9 wins) but trims slightly (Antonelli 0.26 -> 0.25, Russell 0.19 -> 0.18) given Ferrari's convergence and Antonelli's two non-scores in three races. Three-time home winner Max Verstappen trims (0.11 -> 0.09) after suffering his fifth RB22 mechanical/aero disaster of 2026 ('super-dangerous' rear-wing detachment crash at Stowe + unresolved engine power issue), offset by genuine podium pace when running. Top-5 sum = 0.79, leaving 0.21 outside for Norris (~0.085), Piastri (~0.07), Hadjar (~0.025), and post-break upgrades/coastal weather (~0.03).
